key_insight: 360Anything removes the need for camera calibration by using pre-trained diffusion transformers to lift standard perspective images and videos into complete 360° equirectangular panoramas, treating inputs as partial observations to be completed in a learned latent space.
problem_solved: Generates immersive 360° panoramas from in-the-wild images and videos without requiring explicit geometric alignment or camera metadata, making panorama synthesis robust to missing or noisy calibration.
method: Geometry-free formulation: treat perspective input as a partial 360° observation and avoid explicit camera-to-ERP alignment.
Leverage pre-trained diffusion transformers to perform latent-space completion/translation from perspective crops to full equirectangular panoramas.
Support for both images and video by applying the same learned completion mechanism with temporal consistency strategies for video frames.
impact: Enables practitioners to create 360° content from uncalibrated, real-world image/video sources—simplifying pipelines for VR/AR content, novel-view rendering, and immersive dataset creation without tedious camera metadata collection.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: perspective image -> geometry-free diffusion transformer -> completed 360° equirectangular panorama

paper_title: 360Anything: Geometry-Free Lifting of Images and Videos to 360°
paper_authors: Ziyi Wu, Daniel Watson, Andrea Tagliasacchi, David J. Fleet, Marcus A. Brubaker
